scope: Independent scoped correctness review of local artifact parent resolution memo; Linux host, no performance/product acceptance
findings: Original destination function is byte-identical to baseline and remains the cache miss resolver. Parent keys retain ParentDir components; Path normalization of separators/CurDir matches the original components traversal.

Each relative resolve obtains the current working directory before looking up the absolute parent. Filename errors and current_dir errors preserve original ordering. Nonabsolute drive-relative results conservatively call the old destination; this branch is not natively Windows-tested.

Only one successful parent is retained in an automatic local variable: project dependency construction and every validate each instantiate distinct caches. It is absent from CompilationSession, ArtifactPlan and NativePublication, and cannot cross observer callbacks or validation/publication boundaries.

identity still performs metadata on each requested file. Existing files retain regular-file validation, per-file canonicalize and Unix dev/inode extraction; missing files retain per-file dangling-final-symlink rejection before cached parent resolution. Errors are not cached.

ArtifactPlan::new/root ordering, dependency order, source-source overlap/inode conflicts, source-output collisions, repeated dump/native/publication validate, cancellation and atomic publication/rollback logic are unchanged.

For a stable filesystem within a synchronous batch, the final filename cannot affect parent resolution; successful cached-parent concatenation yields the same destination. Concurrent external filesystem mutation has no atomic-snapshot guarantee in either implementation; no stronger race-proof guarantee is claimed.

Linux process_cpu_ns uses CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID with native 64-bit Linux timespec layout. Timing encloses compile_project and includes compiler threads/observer bookkeeping; it excludes child-linker/native-control CPU. CPU boundaries slightly enclose wall boundaries and do not replace wall-clock comparison. Native execution remains after timers.

All benchmark arms must be rebuilt from the same probe source before comparison. Historical phase intervals remain observer intervals, not exclusive CPU attribution. Stage-3 performance numbers added to FRONTEND-REUSE.md were not independently recomputed in this correctness review.
